subject: Crescent Health — SLA measurement, telemetry windows & service credit mechanics
messages:
From: Maxine Carter <maxine.carter@crescenthealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@crescenthealth.com, sanjay.rao@crescenthealth.com
Date: 2026-01-10T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Crescent Health SLA questionnaire — clarification on measurement windows and credits

Dylan,

Thanks for sending the questionnaire. A couple of things our procurement team flagged that need clearer wording before we can include your wording in the RFP appendix:

1) "Burst window" vs "aggregation window" — when you report latency percentiles for SLA compliance, do you evaluate per-minute rolling windows, or is the window aligned to the SLAs' 1-minute / 5-minute buckets? Our auditors need to know if a localized spike will be captured in the same way as an aggregated window.

2) Service credits calculation — does Redwood compute credits using a per-region normalized request volume, or is weighting applied for multi-region routes? If a customer's traffic is split 70/30 across us-east/us-west, how would a short outage in one region be credited?

3) Evidence package — what telemetry artifacts will you provide (raw sample logs, sampling methodology, synthetic probe results)? We have to prepare a handoff checklist to our security and compliance teams.

I've attached the RFP worksheet with our suggested formal wording (crescent_sla_questionnaire_v1.xlsx). Can your team propose a short paragraph for each item (windowing, weighting, evidence) we can place into the master SLA exhibit?

Best,
Maxine
Maxine Carter
Sr. Procurement Manager | Crescent Health

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Crescent Health SLA questionnaire — clarification on measurement windows and credits

Maxine —

Thanks for the clear questions and for the worksheet. Below are short paragraphs you can drop into the exhibit; happy to iterate. I've kept the language concise for legal consumption and added links to sample telemetry in the attachment.

1) Measurement windows: Redwood measures SLA percentiles over aligned 1-minute aggregation buckets by default. For latency SLA evaluation we compute per-request percentiles within each 1-minute bucket and then apply the SLA rule over the billing period (monthly). Short spikes that fully occur within a single 1-minute bucket are counted toward that bucket’s percentile results. We also provide an optional continuous rolling percentile export (sampled) on request for forensic analysis.

2) Regional weighting & crediting: Credits are calculated per-customer by normalizing requests across the configured production regions using observed routed request counts during the measurement period. A partial degradation in one region will be weighted by that region’s fraction of total customer traffic. If the customer configures sticky routing or pinning to a region, the weighting uses the effective routing table for that customer for the period in question.

3) Evidence package: For credit disputes we deliver: (a) raw sampled telemetry for the affected windows (token-level latencies, request IDs, timestamps), (b) probe results and synthetic job traces for the same time window, and (c) routing tables and scaling events from the control plane. Sensitive artifacts are delivered via our secure share with access logs.

Attached: a short telemetry snippet and the marked worksheet.

Next step: if that language looks good, Marissa (legal) and Kim (ops) can sign off and we’ll send a finalized exhibit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if you prefer to talk through edge cases.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks

Hi Maxine / team —

I reviewed Dylan’s proposed paragraphs. A few notes from Legal/Contracts so the language is enforceable and aligns with our billing model:

- Measurement window: we prefer to explicitly state "1-minute aligned aggregation windows (UTC)" to avoid ambiguity about timezone alignment. Please confirm Crescent is fine with UTC-based windowing.

- Weighting: to be explicit, we will calculate credit entitlements by taking the sum of unavailable (or out-of-spec) weighted requests divided by total customer requests in the measurement period, then apply the credit formula in the SLA schedule. We cannot retroactively reassign traffic weights outside of recorded routing tables.

- Evidence delivery: we will provide telemetry as described, with delivery via our secure share and an expiration window of 90 days. If Crescent requires longer retention for dispute evidence, we can add a paid evidence-retention addendum.

I am attaching a suggested redline of your exhibit language (I included a short definitional paragraph for "aggregation window" and "routing table snapshot"). If you accept, we will incorporate into the final SLA exhibit and circulate for signatures.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks — that reads well. Two quick clarifications from our side:

- UTC windows are fine (we'll note in our compliance checklist).
- For audits, do you provide proof of the routing table snapshot (signed/timestamped) showing the fraction of traffic per region? We need the timestamped control-plane snapshot not just the counters.

Also, procurement wants the concrete credit example in the exhibit — a worked example where region A handles 80% and region B 20% and region B falls below availability for 30 minutes, showing the math to compute the percent of impacted requests and resulting credit. Can you provide that as an annex?

If you can send the redline + worked example by Monday we will include in our internal packet to the audit team.

Best,

Subject: Re: Crescent Health SLA questionnaire — clarification on measurement windows and credits

Maxine —

Adding a short operational note and the worked credit example (text below) you can paste into the annex. We will also produce a signed control-plane snapshot (hash + timestamp) as part of the evidence bundle for any credit claim.

Operational note: routing table snapshots are produced every 5 minutes by our control plane and signed with a monotonic sequence number. For an evidence package we include the snapshot(s) that cover the impacted minutes and the signed hash; customers can verify via our signed manifest.

Worked example (annex):
- Period: 2026-01-01 month (example)
- Observed customer requests during incident window: 10,000 total across regions
- Region A routed requests during incident window: 8,000 (80%)
- Region B routed requests during incident window: 2,000 (20%)
- Region B availability in the affected 30-minute window: 0% (complete outage)
- Impacted requests attributable to Region B outage: 2,000 / 10,000 = 20% of traffic
- If the SLA credit table specifies a 10% monthly availability shortfall leading to X credits, then the effective customer credit is prorated by the 20% impacted fraction. Example: if full-service credit for total outage = $10,000, customer receives 20% * $10,000 = $2,000 under the weighting model.

We’ll attach a PDF example with the math and include the signed routing manifests in the evidence pack when requested.

If Crescent wants different math (e.g., region-weighted by capacity rather than observed routed fraction) say so — we can include an alternative annex but it may require different control-plane hooks and a short integration project.

— Karthik Iyer
Director, Cloud Reliability | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: annex-worked-credit-example.pdf (application/pdf)]
